title: Allow using non-password auth method without having to move the mouse first
line: The fingerprint reader now unlocks the screen right away, without having to move the mouse or press a key first.
explanation: The lock screen only armed the fingerprint reader while its UI was shown. When the screen locks the PAM workers are not ready yet, so the first attempt is dropped and nothing armed the reader again until the user woke the UI; since plasma-desktop dead05e8 hiding the UI also cancels it, and once pam_fprintd times out nothing re-arms it. The greeter now arms the separate fingerprint authenticator as soon as its worker is ready, re-arms it whenever its conversation ends, and leaves it running when the UI hides, until the screen is unlocked.

commits.message:
greeter: keep the fingerprint reader armed while the screen is locked

The fingerprint reader was only armed while the lock screen UI was
shown, so touching it did nothing until the mouse was moved. Keep it
armed for as long as the screen is locked and re-arm it on timeout.

BUG: 469810

media.caption: Before: lock, touch nothing, place the finger at 0:22. The screen stays locked (the reader was never armed).
After: same steps. The reader is armed from the start, re-armed after its 15 s timeout, and the finger at 0:22 unlocks.
Before: prompt shown and left to fade out, finger placed after it hid: still locked.
After: same steps, the finger unlocks to the desktop.

reviews.text: Keeping the implicit fingerprint authenticator armed in PamAuthenticators while locked and re-arming it on worker readiness and conversation end is a clean approach that works with LockScreenUi.qml cancelling active auth on hide. However, re-arming unconditionally in the failed slot was only tested across a single 15-second timeout while verify.regressions notes an existing 4-try failure counter, creating a high risk that normal timeouts permanently disable the reader after ~1–2 minutes locked; there are also missing readiness/busy guards and a black-screen after video.
changes: Verify across 5+ consecutive pam_fprintd timeouts (e.g., >75–120 s locked) that PamAuthenticator's existing 4-try failure counter does not mark the fingerprint reader unavailable during normal idle timeouts; if it does, update PamAuthenticator so slow/timeout endings do not trip the rapid-failure disable counter.

Guard armFingerprintAuthenticator() with isReady() and !isBusy() (or equivalent) so readyChanged becoming false and startAuthenticating() on UI wakeup do not redundantly call tryUnlock() on an already-armed or unready worker.

Check and handle (or explicitly document why not) the case where the user explicitly selects Authenticator::Fingerprint in the switcher (persisted by saveAuthenticatorType), since m_fingerprintAuthenticator is null in that mode and m_activeAuthenticator is still cancelled on hide.
Re-record after-1.mp4 so the locked screen (not solid black frames from 0:00–0:23) is visible before the fingerprint touch unlocks it, ideally demonstrating survival past multiple timeouts.
